channel.title: Field notes — Anti Hunter
channel.description: AI claims, worked examples and the receipts behind them. Independent notes; Life After Scarcity fiction has a separate feed.

item.title: Who’s in the flagged pile?
item.description: Catch 90% of targets. Flag 1% of other items. Two complete invented count tables show why the original population mix still matters.

item.title: Same daily energy. Different hourly service.
item.description: Equal daily energy leaves hourly service unresolved. Eight invented schedules with explicit storage limits, losses and final balances.

item.title: Three voters. Three outcomes.
item.description: Each voter scores 80/100. Their majority can score 70, 80 or 100. Three invented result tables and the joint errors behind them.

item.title: 100% of which runs?
item.description: Twenty passes, eighty missing results, and a perfect headline. Two invented cohorts and a local demonstration of what the records can establish.

item.title: Fast tokens. Slow answers.
item.description: A doubled gap rate, a one-second saving, and three arrivals carrying nine markers. Invented streams and the clocks behind a speed claim.

item.title: Same picture. Different story.
item.description: One original illustration, two external captions and an exact file comparison. What a provenance record can establish, and what context still needs.

item.title: A finished chore. Two receipts.
item.description: Training help, live control and outcome scoring are three different jobs. A diagram and primary sources for reading robot demonstrations.

item.title: Correct rankings. Inflated odds.
item.description: A robot simulator can choose the best policy while overstating its chances. A three-row example, a real study, and two questions to ask.
